topic: The Geometry of High-Dimensional Spheres: Beyond 3D
target_audience: University students (STEM majors with basic calculus/linear algebra)

sections.title: Introduction: The Dimensional Leap
lecture_lines: Generalize to n dimensions using the Pythagorean theorem.
This leads to the hypersphere definition.
animations: Display title: "Introduction: The Dimensional Leap" in #FFFFFF.
Show a 2D circle appearing in #FFD700, morphing into a 3D sphere.
Generalize Pythagorean theorem using MathTex: r^2 = \sum x_i^2 in #FFFFFF.
Fade in a 4D hypersphere wireframe representation.
Highlight the 4D center with a glowing #00FFFF point.

sections.title: The Counter-Intuitive Volume Paradox
lecture_lines: Unit spheres shrink as dimensions increase.
We use the Gamma function for calculation.
Imagine a unit sphere in a unit cube.
animations: Show a unit circle in #1E90FF inside a unit square.
Show a unit sphere in #1E90FF inside a unit cube.
Display Gamma function definition: V_n(R) = \frac{\pi^{n/2}}{\Gamma(n/2+1)}R^n in #FFFFFF.
Visualize the unit sphere shrinking compared to the unit cube.
Highlight corner regions in #FF4500 to show volume concentration.

sections.title: The Concentration of Measure
lecture_lines: High dimensions exhibit concentration of measure.
Volume collects in a thin surface shell.
animations: Draw a Gaussian bell curve in #32CD32 showing shell thickness.
Highlight the thin shell surface where points concentrate.

sections.title: Real-World Application: High-Dimensional Data
lecture_lines: Machine learning maps vectors on spheres.
We use cosine similarity to measure distance.
animations: Show data matrix with vectors as arrows in #FFFFFF.
Visualize vectors pointing towards a hypersphere surface.
Calculate cosine similarity between two vectors using MathTex: \frac{A \cdot B}{\|A\|\|B\|}.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
lecture_lines: Hyperspheres are concentrated at the surface.
animations: Display "Volume Paradox" label in #FFFFFF and pulse #00FFFF.
